title: Flush an IV saline lock and clamp its line while the plunger is still pressed
instruction: Flush the IV saline lock with the syringe and clamp the line.
context: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00; about 3.3 million US jobs, BLS May 2024) and licensed practical nurses flush every peripheral IV before and after each use. With a negative-displacement needleless connector, the infusion-therapy standards' sequence is flush, clamp, then disconnect: letting go of the plunger with the line still open lets the syringe's rubber stopper spring back and draw blood into the catheter tip, where it clots and blocks the IV. Unlike tasks that push a syringe or close a clamp alone, the score depends on the order of two hands: the clamp must shut while the other hand is still pushing.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Everything lies along one line at x 30, the syringe on the robot's right. (1) IV training forearm pad: pink skin-tone silicone block 12 x 24 x 3.2 cm (x 24 to 36, y 5 to 29), fixed, with a blue vein line along it. (2) Peripheral IV catheter: clear hub with blue wings, taped to the pad at y 8.6 under a clear film dressing 5 x 3 cm. (3) Extension set: clear PVC tubing 3.6 mm across, from the hub along the pad and off its end to a needleless connector (clear body 1.2 cm across, 2.5 cm long, blue septum cap, a negative-displacement type) at y -3 to -0.5, 3.6 cm above the table, held in a white plastic securement clip (3.2 x 2.2 x 3 cm, fixed to the table). (4) Pinch clamp on the tubing at y 2.2: white plastic, a fixed jaw on the tubing's +x side and a moving jaw on its -x side, each 3 mm thick, 1.4 cm along the tubing and 3 cm tall (2.6 to 5.6 cm up); open at the start (the moving jaw 4.5 mm back from the tubing); squeezed shut, its ratchet teeth catch and hold it. (5) Prefilled saline flush syringe, 10 mL barrel (14.5 mm bore, 16.5 mm outside, clear with a printed scale) holding 5 mL of 0.9% saline, screwed onto the connector and pointing toward -y: finger flange at y -11.5, rubber stopper at the 5 mL mark, white plunger rod with a 22 mm thumb press (3 mm thick) whose back face is at y -16.0, 3.6 cm up. The plunger moves 3.0 cm (6.05 mm per mL) to empty the syringe.
scoring: Let go under pressure, latched: 0 if, at any time, a gripper comes off the plunger (its thumb press or its rod, whichever it was holding) for 0.15 s or more after pushing the plunger in at least 0.1 mL during that contact while the clamp is still open; the stopper springs back and draws blood into the catheter tip. In a real trial, check on the video that the clamp's teeth had caught before the pushing gripper left the thumb press or rod, and look for blood in the clear hub. At the end, also 0 if a gripper still touches the thumb press, the rod or the clamp (within 2 mm; video), if the plunger or the clamp jaw is still moving faster than 2 mm/s, or if the clamp is not shut (its teeth caught; the 4.5 mm jaw travel done). Otherwise by the saline flushed, read from the syringe's printed scale (6.05 mm of plunger per mL): 1.0 at 4.8 mL or more (the whole 5 mL syringe, the plunger within 1.2 mm of the barrel's end); 0.5 at 3.0 mL or more (over twice the line's volume of about 1.2 mL); 0.25 at 1.0 mL or more; 0 below 1.0 mL. Doing nothing, clamping first (the closed line locks the plunger) or pushing without clamping score 0. Where the arms end up does not count. The final state must hold 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Fit a new prefilled 5 mL flush syringe (the old one is spent), or refill the used barrel to the 5 mL mark and refit it; open the pinch clamp by flexing its ratchet tab. In the real rig, run the line to waste so it is full of saline, and keep the training arm's simulated blood bag at about 10 cm head so reflux shows in the clear hub.
fidelity: No fluid is simulated. The plunger slides on a damper standing for flow out through the catheter (about 1.5 N per 1 mL/s; flow falls with the square of the clamp's opening; a shut clamp locks the plunger) and cannot be drawn back. Stopper spring-back is not simulated: letting go of the plunger (thumb press or rod) with the clamp open is logged as reflux. The clamp and tubing are fixed to the base; a real extension set hangs freely.
